change: Window task partitioning accepts execution budget/result ownership options. Sparse buckets, row copies, copied ordinals and result directories are admitted before construction. Partition expressions use scoped evaluation and existing scalar snapshot normalization plus stable-key admission; temporary keys are released per row. Parquet forwards its caller budget into partitioning. The common synchronous result-scope helper now supports records as well as arrays.

edgeCases: measured partition peak succeeds, peak minus one rejects without leaked charges
oversized replace expression rejects under 64 KiB
100 key probes release all scratch each time
existing large sparse bucket, mutable payload, ordering and Parquet task fixtures

remaining: Parquet scan buffers and partial lifetime across asynchronous task completion remain unowned; partition construction admission does not close that lifecycle gap.
Transport replacement allocation and core scanner owned-task capability remain open.
No whole-query or production Worker heap cap is claimed.
